title: The constructible cocone is a filtered 2-colimit
statement:
Let $\ell$ be a prime and $X$ a scheme whose underlying topological space is Noetherian. The
constructible cocone $E\mapsto D_{\mathrm{cons}}(X,E)\to D_{\mathrm{cons}}(X,\Qlb)$
([def-sfb-constructible-cocone]) is a filtered 2-colimit in the sense of
[sk-def-sfb-filtered-two-colimit].

proof.text: Use [def-sfb-constructible-cocone] to write $\mathcal C_E=D_{\mathrm{cons}}(X,E)$, $\mathcal D=D_{\mathrm{cons}}(X,\Qlb)$, $\Phi_E=T_{E,\Qlb}$ and $\theta_{EF}\colon\Phi_F\circ T_{E,F}\cong\Phi_E$. These are exactly the cocone data to which [sk-def-sfb-filtered-two-colimit] applies; its predicate asks for (Obj), (Hom-surj) and (Hom-inj).

source.place: Assembly of the three defining conditions; unit sk-thm-sfb-qlbar-two-colimit, proof (4)

proof.text: For any $K\in\mathcal D$, [lem-sfb-constructible-cocone-obj] gives a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ in $\Qlb$, an object $K_E\in\mathcal C_E$ and an isomorphism $K\cong\Phi_E(K_E)$. The lemma applies since $\ell$ is prime and the underlying topological space of $X$ is Noetherian. This is (Obj) for our cocone.

source.place: Assembly of the three defining conditions; unit sk-thm-sfb-qlbar-two-colimit, proof (4)

proof.text: Fix finite stages $E,F$, objects $K_E\in\mathcal C_E$, $L_F\in\mathcal C_F$, and a morphism $\varphi\colon\Phi_E(K_E)\to\Phi_F(L_F)$. Under the same hypotheses, [lem-sfb-constructible-cocone-hom-surj] gives a finite $H\supseteq E,F$ and $g\colon T_{E,H}K_E\to T_{F,H}L_F$ whose image is $\varphi$ up to the transitivity isomorphisms. In the notation of step 1 this equality is $\varphi=\theta_{FH,L_F}\circ\Phi_H(g)\circ\theta_{EH,K_E}^{-1}$. The inverse first carries $\Phi_E(K_E)$ to $\Phi_H(T_{E,H}K_E)$, and the last isomorphism carries $\Phi_H(T_{F,H}L_F)$ to $\Phi_F(L_F)$. Thus the equality is precisely (Hom-surj), including its comparison maps.

source.place: Assembly of the three defining conditions; unit sk-thm-sfb-qlbar-two-colimit, proof (4)

proof.text: Fix a finite stage $H$, $K,L\in\mathcal C_H$, and $g,g^{\prime}\colon K\to L$ with $\Phi_H(g)=\Phi_H(g^{\prime})$. The hypotheses of [lem-sfb-constructible-cocone-hom-inj] are exactly these together with the prime and Noetherian hypotheses already in force. It gives a finite $H^{\prime}\supseteq H$ with $T_{H,H^{\prime}}(g)=T_{H,H^{\prime}}(g^{\prime})$. This is (Hom-inj).

source.place: Assembly of the three defining conditions; unit sk-thm-sfb-qlbar-two-colimit, proof (4)

proof.text: Steps 2, 3 and 4 supply respectively (Obj), (Hom-surj) and (Hom-inj) for the single cocone fixed in step 1. Their conjunction is the definition of a filtered 2-colimit in [sk-def-sfb-filtered-two-colimit]. Therefore the constructible cocone is a filtered 2-colimit as asserted. This last step is only introduction of the three fields of that predicate.
